clues: This place stands where a wide river drops over rocks in rapids. Boats from the sea can sail up no farther than this spot.
High hills to the west slow down blasts of cold air from the far north. The cold air warms up as it sinks down toward this place.
In 1780 the seat of government moved here from the old port town of Williamsburg. The new spot sat more in the center, safe from sea attack.
In 1775, in a small church here, Patrick Henry cried out for freedom. His words, give me liberty or give me death, still ring out today.
Virginia state government runs from this place. Its lawmakers and its governor do their work here.
